NKJV.1: The lot fell to the children of Joseph from the Jordan, by Jericho, to the waters of Jericho on the east, to the wilderness that goes up from Jericho through the mountains to Bethel,
NKJV.2: then went out from Bethel to Luz, passed along to the border of the Archites at Ataroth,
NKJV.3: and went down westward to the boundary of the Japhletites, as far as the boundary of Lower Beth Horon to Gezer; and it ended at the sea.
NKJV.4: So the children of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, took their inheritance.
NKJV.5: The border of the children of Ephraim, according to their families, was thus: The border of their inheritance on the east side was Ataroth Addar as far as Upper Beth Horon.
NKJV.6: And the border went out toward the sea on the north side of Michmethath; then the border went around eastward to Taanath Shiloh, and passed by it on the east of Janohah.
NKJV.7: Then it went down from Janohah to Ataroth and Naarah, reached to Jericho, and came out at the Jordan.
NKJV.8: The border went out from Tappuah westward to the Brook Kanah, and it ended at the sea. This was the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Ephraim according to their families.
NKJV.9: The separate cities for the children of Ephraim were among the inheritance of the children of Manasseh, all the cities with their villages.
NKJV.10: And they did not drive out the Canaanites who dwelt in Gezer; but the Canaanites dwell among the Ephraimites to this day and have become forced laborers.

NASB.1: Then the lot for the sons of Joseph went from the Jordan at Jericho to the waters of Jericho on the east into the wilderness, going up from Jericho through the hill country to Bethel.
NASB.2: It went from Bethel to Luz, and continued to the border of the Archites at Ataroth.
NASB.3: It went down westward to the territory of the Japhletites, as far as the territory of lower Beth-horon even to Gezer, and it ended at the sea.
NASB.4: The sons of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, received their inheritance.
NASB.5: Now [this] was the territory of the sons of Ephraim according to their families: the border of their inheritance eastward was Ataroth-addar, as far as upper Beth-horon.
NASB.6: Then the border went westward at Michmethath on the north, and the border turned about eastward to Taanath-shiloh and continued [beyond] it to the east of Janoah.
NASB.7: It went down from Janoah to Ataroth and to Naarah, then reached Jericho and came out at the Jordan.
NASB.8: From Tappuah the border continued westward to the brook of Kanah, and it ended at the sea. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Ephraim according to their families,
NASB.9: [together] with the cities which were set apart for the sons of Ephraim in the midst of the inheritance of the sons of Manasseh, all the cities with their villages.
NASB.10: But they did not drive out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, so the Canaanites live in the midst of Ephraim to this day, and they became forced laborers.

ESV.1: The allotment of the people of Joseph went from the Jordan by Jericho, east of the waters of Jericho, into the wilderness, going up from Jericho into the hill country to Bethel.
ESV.2: Then going from Bethel to Luz, it passes along to Ataroth, the territory of the Archites.
ESV.3: Then it goes down westward to the territory of the Japhletites, as far as the territory of Lower Beth-horon, then to Gezer, and it ends at the sea.
ESV.4: The people of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, received their inheritance.
ESV.5: The territory of the people of Ephraim by their clans was as follows: the boundary of their inheritance on the east was Ataroth-addar as far as Upper Beth-horon,
ESV.6: and the boundary goes from there to the sea. On the north is Michmethath. Then on the east the boundary turns around toward Taanath-shiloh and passes along beyond it on the east to Janoah,
ESV.7: then it goes down from Janoah to Ataroth and to Naarah, and touches Jericho, ending at the Jordan.
ESV.8: From Tappuah the boundary goes westward to the brook Kanah and ends at the sea. Such is the inheritance of the tribe of the people of Ephraim by their clans,
ESV.9: together with the towns that were set apart for the people of Ephraim within the inheritance of the Manassites, all those towns with their villages.
ESV.10: However, they did not drive out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, so the Canaanites have lived in the midst of Ephraim to this day but have been made to do forced labor.

CSB17.1: The allotment for the descendants of Joseph went from the Jordan at Jericho to the Waters of Jericho on the east, through the wilderness <sup>ⓔ</sup> ascending from Jericho into the hill country of Bethel.
CSB17.2: From Bethel it went to Luz and proceeded to the border of the Archites by Ataroth. <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.3: It then descended westward to the border of the Japhletites as far as the border of lower Beth-horon, then to Gezer, <sup>ⓖ</sup> and ended at the Mediterranean Sea.
CSB17.4: So Ephraim and Manasseh, the sons of Joseph, <sup>ⓗ</sup> received their inheritance. <sup>ⓘ</sup>
CSB17.5: This was the territory of the descendants of Ephraim by their clans: The border of their inheritance went from Ataroth-addar <sup>ⓙ</sup> on the east to Upper Beth-horon.
CSB17.6: In the north the border went westward from Michmethath; <sup>ⓚ</sup> it turned eastward from Taanath-shiloh and passed it east of Janoah.
CSB17.7: From Janoah it descended to Ataroth and Naarah, <sup>ⓛ</sup> and then reached Jericho and went to the Jordan.
CSB17.8: From Tappuah the border went westward along the Brook of Kanah and ended at the Mediterranean Sea. <sup>ⓜ</sup> This was the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Ephraim by their clans, together with
CSB17.9: the cities set apart for the descendants of Ephraim within the inheritance of the descendants of Manasseh — all these cities with their settlements.
CSB17.10: However, they did not drive out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer. <sup>ⓝ</sup> So the Canaanites still live in Ephraim today, <sup>ⓐ</sup> but they are forced laborers.

WEB.1: The lot came out for the children of Joseph from the Jordan at Jericho, at the waters of Jericho on the east, even the wilderness, going up from Jericho through the hill country to Bethel.
WEB.2: It went out from Bethel to Luz, and passed along to the border of the Archites to Ataroth;
WEB.3: and it went down westward to the border of the Japhletites, to the border of Beth Horon the lower, and on to Gezer; and ended at the sea.
WEB.4: The children of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, took their inheritance.
WEB.5: This was the border of the children of Ephraim according to their families. The border of their inheritance eastward was Ataroth Addar, to Beth Horon the upper.
WEB.6: The border went out westward at Michmethath on the north. The border turned about eastward to Taanath Shiloh, and passed along it on the east of Janoah.
WEB.7: It went down from Janoah to Ataroth, to Naarah, reached to Jericho, and went out at the Jordan.
WEB.8: From Tappuah the border went along westward to the brook of Kanah; and ended at the sea. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Ephraim according to their families;
WEB.9: together with the cities which were set apart for the children of Ephraim in the middle of the inheritance of the children of Manasseh, all the cities with their villages.
WEB.10: They didn’t drive out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer; but the Canaanites dwell in the territory of Ephraim to this day, and have become servants to do forced labor.

NLT.1: The allotment for the descendants of Joseph extended from the Jordan River near Jericho, east of the springs of Jericho, through the wilderness and into the hill country of Bethel.
NLT.2: From Bethel (that is, Luz) it ran over to Ataroth in the territory of the Arkites.
NLT.3: Then it descended westward to the territory of the Japhletites as far as Lower Beth-horon, then to Gezer and over to the Mediterranean Sea.
NLT.4: This was the homeland allocated to the families of Joseph’s sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
NLT.5: The following territory was given to the clans of the tribe of Ephraim. The boundary of their homeland began at Ataroth-addar in the east. From there it ran to Upper Beth-horon,
NLT.6: then on to the Mediterranean Sea. From Micmethath on the north, the boundary curved eastward past Taanath-shiloh to the east of Janoah.
NLT.7: From Janoah it turned southward to Ataroth and Naarah, touched Jericho, and ended at the Jordan River.
NLT.8: From Tappuah the boundary extended westward, following the Kanah Ravine to the Mediterranean Sea. This is the homeland allocated to the clans of the tribe of Ephraim.
NLT.9: In addition, some towns with their surrounding villages in the territory allocated to the half-tribe of Manasseh were set aside for the tribe of Ephraim.
NLT.10: They did not drive the Canaanites out of Gezer, however, so the people of Gezer live as slaves among the people of Ephraim to this day.

AMP.1: Then the lot (allotment) for the sons of Joseph went from the Jordan Valley at Jericho to the waters of Jericho on the east into the wilderness, going up from Jericho through the hill country to Bethel.
AMP.2: Then it went from Bethel to Luz, and continued to Ataroth, the border of the Archites.
AMP.3: It went down westward to the territory of the Japhletites, as far as the outskirts of lower Beth-horon, then to Gezer, and it ended at the sea.
AMP.4: The sons of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, received their inheritance.
AMP.5: Now this was the territory of the sons of Ephraim according to their families: on the east side the border of their inheritance was Ataroth-addar, as far as upper Beth-horon.
AMP.6: Then the border went westward at Michmethath on the north, and turned eastward to Taanath-shiloh and continued beyond it to the east of Janoah.
AMP.7: It went down from Janoah to Ataroth and to Naarah, touched Jericho and ended at the Jordan.
AMP.8: The border continued from Tappuah westward to the Brook Kanah, and it ended at the [Mediterranean] sea. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Ephraim according to their families (clans),
AMP.9: with the cities which were set apart for the sons of Ephraim within the inheritance of the sons of Manasseh, all the cities with their villages.
AMP.10: But they did not drive out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, so the Canaanites live among Ephraim to this day, and they became forced laborers.

NIV.1:
Allotment for Ephraim and Manasseh
The allotment for Joseph began at the Jordan of Jericho, east of the waters of Jericho, and went up from there through the desert into the hill country of Bethel.
NIV.2: It went on from Bethel (that is, Luz), crossed over to the territory of the Arkites in Ataroth,
NIV.3: descended westward to the territory of the Japhletites as far as the region of Lower Beth Horon and on to Gezer, ending at the sea.
NIV.4: So Manasseh and Ephraim, the descendants of Joseph, received their inheritance.
NIV.5:
This was the territory of Ephraim, clan by clan:
The boundary of their inheritance went from Ataroth Addar in the east to Upper Beth Horon
NIV.6: and continued to the sea. From Micmethath on the north it curved eastward to Taanath Shiloh, passing by it to Janoah on the east.
NIV.7: Then it went down from Janoah to Ataroth and Naarah, touched Jericho and came out at the Jordan.
NIV.8: From Tappuah the border went west to the Kanah Ravine and ended at the sea. This was the inheritance of the tribe of the Ephraimites, clan by clan.
NIV.9: It also included all the towns and their villages that were set aside for the Ephraimites within the inheritance of the Manassites.
NIV.10: They did not dislodge the Canaanites living in Gezer; to this day the Canaanites live among the people of Ephraim but are required to do forced labor.

MSG.1: The lot for the people of Joseph went from the Jordan near Jericho, east of the spring of Jericho, north through the desert mountains to Bethel.
MSG.2: It went on from Bethel (that is, Luz) to the territory of the Arkites in Ataroth.
MSG.3: It then descended westward to the territory of the Japhletites to the region of Lower Beth Horon and on to Gezer, ending at the Sea.
MSG.4: This is the region from which the people of Joseph—Manasseh and Ephraim—got their inheritance.
MSG.5:
Ephraim's territory by clans:
The boundary of their inheritance went from Ataroth Addar in the east to Upper Beth Horon
MSG.6: and then west to the Sea. From Micmethath on the north it turned eastward to Taanath Shiloh and passed along, still eastward, to Janoah.
MSG.7: The border then descended from Janoah to Ataroth and Naarah; it touched Jericho and came out at the Jordan.
MSG.8: From Tappuah the border went westward to the Brook Kanah and ended at the Sea. This was the inheritance of the tribe of Ephraim by clans,
MSG.9: including the cities set aside for Ephraim within the inheritance of Manasseh—all those towns and their villages.
MSG.10: But they didn't get rid of the Canaanites who were living in Gezer. Canaanites are still living among the people of Ephraim, but they are made to do forced labor.

NRSVCE.2: then going from Bethel to Luz, it passes along to Ataroth, the territory of the Archites;
NRSVCE.3: then it goes down westward to the territory of the Japhletites, as far as the territory of Lower Beth-horon, then to Gezer, and it ends at the sea.
NRSVCE.4: The Josephites — Manasseh and Ephraim — received their inheritance.
NRSVCE.5: The territory of the Ephraimites by their families was as follows: the boundary of their inheritance on the east was Ataroth-addar as far as Upper Beth-horon,
NRSVCE.6: and the boundary goes from there to the sea; on the north is Michmethath; then on the east the boundary makes a turn toward Taanath-shiloh, and passes along beyond it on the east to Janoah,
NRSVCE.7: then it goes down from Janoah to Ataroth and to Naarah, and touches Jericho, ending at the Jordan.
NRSVCE.8: From Tappuah the boundary goes westward to the Wadi Kanah, and ends at the sea. Such is the inheritance of the tribe of the Ephraimites by their families,
NRSVCE.9: together with the towns that were set apart for the Ephraimites within the inheritance of the Manassites, all those towns with their villages.
NRSVCE.10: They did not, however, drive out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer: so the Canaanites have lived within Ephraim to this day but have been made to do forced labor.

NET.1: The land allotted to Joseph’s descendants extended from the Jordan at Jericho to the waters of Jericho to the east, through the desert and on up from Jericho into the hill country of Bethel.
NET.2: The southern border extended from Bethel to Luz, and crossed to Arkite territory at Ataroth.
NET.3: It then descended westward to Japhletite territory, as far as the territory of lower Beth Horon and Gezer, and ended at the sea.
NET.4: Joseph’s descendants, Manasseh and Ephraim, were assigned their land.
NET.5: The territory of the tribe of Ephraim by its clans included the following: The border of their assigned land to the east was Ataroth Addar as far as upper Beth Horon.
NET.6: It then extended on to the sea, with Micmethath on the north. It turned eastward to Taanath Shiloh and crossed it on the east to Janoah.
NET.7: It then descended from Janoah to Ataroth and Naarah, touched Jericho, and extended to the Jordan River.
NET.8: From Tappuah it went westward to the Valley of Kanah and ended at the sea. This is the land assigned to the tribe of Ephraim by its clans.
NET.9: Also included were the cities set apart for the tribe of Ephraim within Manasseh’s territory, along with their towns.
NET.10: The Ephraimites did not conquer the Canaanites living in Gezer. The Canaanites live among the Ephraimites to this very day and do hard labor as their servants.
